subject: creative-arts-and-sports
general_outcomes: perform and display different Creative Arts works to promote diverse cultural knowledge and expression
create artworks to share their ideas, emotions, thoughts, feelings and experiences for learning and enjoyment
perform physical and health activities for enjoyment, survival and self-fulfilment
apply environmental conservation values of re-use and recycle of materials for creative and improvisation purposes
evaluate Creative Arts works to make meaningful connections to creating, executing, performing, display and appreciation of art works
use emerging technologies as a learning tool to explore creative ideas in the process of making, performing, displaying and appreciation of Creative Arts’ works
acquire a variety of developmentally appropriate Creative Arts experiences within the social, cultural, national and international contexts
address pertinent and contemporary issues in society through Creative Arts’ works.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to create and/or execute:  a rhythmic pattern using an indigenous percussion musical instrument,  a drawing using smudge technique,  passing skills in Netball  catching skills in Netball  a montage on ball games
assessment_rubric.exceeds: Creates and/or executes the 9 items in Creative activities correctly and aesthetically.
assessment_rubric.meets: Creates and/or executes the 9 items in Creative activities correctly.
assessment_rubric.approaches: Creates and/or executes the 5-8 items in Creative activities correctly.
assessment_rubric.below: Creates and/or executes the 4 and below items in Creative activities correctly.

substrands.name: Percussion Musical Instruments (Drawing)
learning_outcomes: identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities
classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments
discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument
improvise rhythmic patterns using indigenous percussion musical instruments
make charcoal sticks for drawing
create tonal value on a drawing of a percussion
instrument using the smudging technique
appreciate indigenous percussion instruments from Kenyan communities and pictures drawn.
learning_experiences: watch virtual or actual percussion musical instruments to identify by; name, community and method of playing
observe/listen to sounds of percussion musical instruments and classify as melodic or non-melodic
identify parts of a percussion musical instrument and discuss their function(s) in sound production
practice improvising rhythmic patterns to accompany songs using percussion instruments
talk about value/ tone as an element of art created on virtual and actual sample pictures
collaboratively, collect materials and tools to make charcoal sticks following the correct procedure while observing safety
use charcoal sticks to illustrate how to create tone/value by smudging technique
draw using charcoal sticks a picture of one percussion instrument and create tonal variation by smudging technique
show and talk about own and peers’ percussion instruments and drawings in a just and fair manner.
inquiry_questions: 1. What is the importance of percussion instruments from different communities in Kenya?
2. How is tonal variation created in a drawing?
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learner speaks clearly and listens keenly while talking about their work and working together to make charcoal sticks.
Digital literacy: The learner interacts with digital devices to source information on percussion instruments.
values: Social justice: The learner talks about own and others’ pictures justly.
Responsibility: The learner cares for own and peers’ items and observes safety precautions when making charcoal sticks.

substrands.name: Netball
learning_outcomes: discuss the skills of passing and catching in Netball
make a ball using macramé technique
perform the skills of passing, and catching in Netball
appreciate Netball as a team game for enjoyment.
learning_experiences: watch a virtual or live Netball game and identify passes and catching skills
demonstrate passing (chest and overhead) and catching (double-handed) skills
collect reusable materials and improvise balls using macramé technique (overhand knot)
practise passing (chest and overhead) and catching (double-handed) skills
play a Mini-Netball game applying the skills of (passing and catching) while observing safety
talk about own and others’ skills in Netball game.
inquiry_questions: 1. Why are the skills of passing and catching important in a Netball game?
2. Why is it necessary to improvise a netball?
core_competencies: Creativity and Imagination: The learner explores with varied materials when improvising balls.
Learning to learn: The learner watches a Netball game to learn the netball skills through demonstration and practise.
values: Social justice: The learner demonstrates fairness as they take turns in practising the netball skills of shooting, catching and passing.
Responsibility: The learner takes initiative to clean the working area and store the balls in an improvised storage.
pertinent_issues: Resource mobilisation and utilisation: The learner collects locally available materials to improvise a netball.
Self-esteem: The learner displays confidence in demonstrating new skills through practice and playing a Netball game.
links_to_other_areas: Mathematics: The learner takes part in passing the Netball to a team-mate while applying ball trajectory visualisation.

substrands.name: Painting and Montage
learning_outcomes: classify colours into primary and secondary for painting
paint a picture of simple items for colour value application
create a montage composition for expression
appreciate painting and montage as methods of making pictures.
learning_experiences: mix primary colours to create secondary colours
mix white with a secondary colour to create light tones on a scale strip
mix black with a secondary colour to create dark tones on a scale strip
draw a single object and paint with emphasis on colour value
observe sample montage pictures for familiarity
source picture of ball games and cut out
arrange and paste cut out pictures to make a montage themed “ball games” and clean the working area
• show and take turns to talk about their own and others work.
inquiry_questions: 1. How is glue for pasting pictures improvised?
2. Why is colour classification important in painting?
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups and speaks clearly about their own and others work.
Creativity and Imagination: The learner makes thoughtful choices when producing a montage pictorial composition.
values: Respect: The learner accommodates others’ views during critique of their own and others’ painting and montage work.
Love: The learner takes turns to talk about their own and others work.
pertinent_issues: Social Cohesion: The learner acquires the skill of working with others during creating a montage composition.
links_to_other_areas: Mathematics: The learner mixes colours in correct proportions to classify as primary or secondary colours.

substrands.name: Rhythm
learning_outcomes: interpret rhythmic patterns involving the crotchet, pair of quaver and their rests
write the French rhythm names using free hand lettering
describe the qualities of a good rhythmic pattern
compose a rhythmic pattern involving a crochet, a pair of quavers and their rests
enjoy creating rhythmic patterns.
learning_experiences: listen to/sing familiar topical songs and identify the music notes and their rests using their French rhythm names
clap the rhythm of the songs while reciting their rhythms using French rhythm names
write letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand lettering-ascenders and descenders
use free hand lettering to write French rhythm names taa and ta-te
relate the French rhythm names taa, and ta-te to
music note symbols for crotchet and a pair of quavers
discuss the techniques used in composing rhythmic patterns
write rhythmic patterns from dictation using either French rhythm names or note symbols and their rests
compose original rhythmic patterns and write them using French rhythm names, note symbols and their rests
critique rhythms created by self and peers respecting each other’s views.
inquiry_questions: 1. How can a rhythm be created?
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups and speaks clearly during critique of own and others’ rhythms.
Creativity and Imagination: The learner composes original rhythmic patterns and writes them using French rhythm names, note symbols and their rests.
values: Values:
Respect: The learner accommodates others’ views during critique of own and others’ original rhythmic compositions.
Integrity: The learner creates own original rhythmic patterns. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs):
Social Cohesion: The learner acquires the skill of working with others during group composition of rhythmic patterns.
Social Justice: The learner fairly critiques rhythms created by others and self. Link to other learning areas:
English: The learner applies the concept of syllabic division in reciting French rhythm names of words and writing letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand.
Mathematics: The learner uses the concept of numbers when relating the value of the quaver in relation to the crotchet.

substrands.name: Melody
learning_outcomes: identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody
interpret hand signs for the sol-fa syllables d r m for pitch discrimination
state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition
create short melodies using the sol-fa syllables
model clay slabs with sol-fa syllables using coil and slab techniques
enjoy creating short melodies and modelling using clay.
learning_experiences: sing familiar songs based on the sol-fa syllables d r m, and identify the sol-fa syllables by ear
listen to and identify aurally and orally the sol-fa pitches (d r m) as sounded on a melodic instrument/voice
watch videos/demonstrations of execution of the Kodaly hand signs for the sol-fa syllables d, r m and practice performing the hand signs
brainstorm on the qualities of a good melody
apply composition techniques to create short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m and the note
symbols; crotchet, a pair of quavers and their rests
collect clay for modelling from the local environment
roll clay into slab and cut out three rectangular pieces of three different sizes
model so-lfa syllables (d r m) using coil technique and attach on the slabs.
inquiry_questions: How can interesting melodies be created?
core_competencies: Creativity and Imagination: The learner uses unique and new ideas to compose melodies and models the sol-fa syllables.
Self-efficacy: The learner models the sol-fa syllables and composes original melodies.
values: Unity: The learner works with peers when modelling, creating and performing various melodies.
Love: The learner respects others while critiquing their performances.
value  a rhythmic pattern using French rhythm names and music note symbols and rests,  model clay slabs with sol-fa syllables  short melodies using the sol-fa syllables d r m
pertinent_issues: Life skills: The learner acquires interpersonal skills through interacting with peers in groups as they model sol-fa syllables and create melodies.
Mentorship and peer education: The learner shares their compositions with peers who give feedback for improvement.

substrands.name: Athletics
learning_outcomes: discuss the sprint starts and sprinting techniques
perform the sprint starts and sprinting techniques for skill development
paint the Kenyan flag for an athletic event
recognise the value of flying the Kenyan flag during an athletics event.
learning_experiences: watch a virtual or live demonstration of sprint starts and sprinting techniques
demonstrate a medium and elongated sprint start techniques
demonstrate the sprinting technique
sketch the Kenyan flag on a paper/fabric
paint the flag observing colour arrangement and neatness
attach the flag to a suitable handle
practise the medium and elongated start
practise sprinting technique
run sprint races while observing safety and cheering each other using the flags made
inquiry_questions: 1. Why is it important to maintain appropriate posture during sprints?
2. Why is the national flag flown during a national athletic event?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:
Citizenship: The learner understands sense of belonging to their country as they paint and fly the Kenyan flag.
Digital literacy: The learner uses digital technology to watch a virtual demonstration of sprint starts and sprinting techniques. Values:
Patriotism: The learner appreciates sketching and painting the Kenyan flag.
Love: The learner works with peers to demonstrate the techniques of starting sprints and sprinting techniques. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs):
Safety and security: The learner performs sprints while observing the safety of self and others.

Social cohesion: The learner works with peers as they play sprint games while observing safety and cheering each other using the flags. Link to other learning areas: Social studies: The learner links knowledge of Kenyan flag learnt in Social Studies as they learn colours of the flag.

demonstrate a side roll

Love: The learner takes turn to support a peer during performance of the crab balance and side roll.

Safety: The learner observes safety of self and others as they perform the rolls and balances.

Social cohesion: The learner works in pairs to perform the side roll and crab balance. Link to other learning areas: Mathematics: The learner uses number and sequence concept in performing gymnastics.

links_to_other_areas: Link to other learning areas: Indigenous Languages: The Learner uses indigenous language when singing songs drawn from different communities in Kenya.

core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: The learner uses digital devices to search and watch how to play notes on the descant recorder.

Respect: The learner listens to and accommodates peers’ views during discussions.

Communicable diseases: The learner prevents spread of communicable diseases by observation of hygiene measures in the use of the descant recorder.

Social cohesion: The learner plays the descant recorder in harmony with peers in a group. Link to other learning areas: Agriculture: The learner applies the concepts and knowledge learnt on prevention of communicable diseases in the use of the descant recorder.
